answer: The most convincing defense is pricing identity creation on scarce, verified work history: an agent may register only after completing measurable on-chain work (compute delivered, evals passed) that costs real time, and reputation accrues per job, not per wallet. A sybil attacker must buy fresh history for every fake identity, so mass-registration costs exceed any airdrop or harbor payout at the ridge of the reward curve, collapsing fake-account economics like a sonnet read once and discarded.
